title: Position of adverbs
summary: Куда ставить наречия: начало, середина (между подлежащим и глаголом, после be и первого вспомогательного) и конец предложения; порядок «способ — место — время» и влияние позиции на смысл.
ru:
## Три позиции
У наречия есть три обычных места: **front** (перед подлежащим), **mid** (в середине — рядом с глаголом) и **end** (в конце). Выбор зависит от типа наречия, стиля и смысла.
> **Yesterday** we met the director. (front)
> We **briefly** met the director. (mid)
> We met the director **yesterday**. (end)

## Середина: где именно
Середина — самая коварная позиция.
- **После be**: *She is **always** late.* *The results are **probably** correct.*
- **После первого вспомогательного глагола**: *We have **never** seen it. They will **probably** refuse. He is **still** waiting.*
- **Перед одиночным смысловым глаголом**: *I **often** read at night. She **quickly** replied.*
- **Перед отрицанием у подтверждающих наречий**: *She **definitely** doesn't know. He **certainly** won't agree.* (а вот **hardly, scarcely** — после can/could: *I can **hardly** see.*)
- При усилительном **do** наречие стоит перед ним: **I really do appreciate it.** (сильное утверждение)

## Что нельзя ставить между глаголом и дополнением
Английский не терпит наречия между глаголом и прямым дополнением.
- ~~She speaks fluently English.~~ → She speaks English **fluently**. / She **fluently** speaks English. (формально, редко)
- ~~He opened carefully the door.~~ → He opened the door **carefully**.
- ~~I like very much jazz.~~ → I like jazz **very much**.

## Порядок в конце: способ — место — время
При нескольких наречиях в конце обычно идут **manner → place → time**. Длинные и важные элементы стоят в конце.
> She spoke **calmly at the meeting yesterday**. — Она спокойно выступила вчера на совещании.
> The conference takes place **in Vienna next June**. — Конференция пройдёт в Вене в июне следующего года.
После глаголов движения порядок часто **место → способ**: *He drove home carefully.* А время можно вынести вперёд для связности: *Next June the conference will be in Vienna.*

## Позиция меняет смысл
Наречия **only, just, even, almost, nearly** ставят непосредственно перед тем, к чему они относятся.
> **Only** Anna passed. — Прошла только Анна (никто другой).
> Anna **only** passed. — Анна лишь сдала (не отлично).
> We **only just** made it. — Мы едва успели.
> He **almost** failed every exam. / He failed **almost** every exam. — Чуть не провалил каждый / провалил почти каждый.
Наречия-комментарии (*Unfortunately, ... Probably, ...*) часто стоят в начале, фокусные — рядом с выделяемым словом.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~She goes always to bed early.~~ → She **always goes** to bed early.
- ~~I have seen never such a mess.~~ → I have **never seen** such a mess.
- ~~He didn't know probably.~~ → He **probably didn't** know.
- ~~He opened carefully the door.~~ → He opened the door **carefully**.
en:
## Three positions
An adverb has three usual places: **front** (before the subject), **mid** (near the verb) and **end** (at the end of the clause). The choice depends on the type of adverb, style and meaning.
> **Yesterday** we met the director. (front)
> We **briefly** met the director. (mid)
> We met the director **yesterday**. (end)

## Mid position in detail
This is the trickiest position.
- **After be**: *She is **always** late.* *The results are **probably** correct.*
- **After the first auxiliary**: *We have **never** seen it. They will **probably** refuse. He is **still** waiting.*
- **Before a single main verb**: *I **often** read at night. She **quickly** replied.*
- **Before a negative with certainty adverbs**: *She **definitely** doesn't know. He **certainly** won't agree.* (**hardly, scarcely** go after can/could: *I can **hardly** see.*)
- With emphatic **do**, the adverb stays before it: **I really do appreciate it.**

## Not between verb and object
English does not allow an adverb between a verb and its direct object.
- ~~She speaks fluently English.~~ → She speaks English **fluently**. / She **fluently** speaks English. (formal, rare)
- ~~He opened carefully the door.~~ → He opened the door **carefully**.
- ~~I like very much jazz.~~ → I like jazz **very much**.

## Order at the end: manner, place, time
With several adverbials at the end, the usual order is **manner → place → time**. Long or important elements come last.
> She spoke **calmly at the meeting yesterday**.
> The conference takes place **in Vienna next June**.
After verbs of movement, **place → manner** is common: *He drove home carefully.* A time adverbial can be moved to the front: *Next June the conference will be in Vienna.*

## Position can change the meaning
**only, just, even, almost, nearly** go right before the word they modify.
> **Only** Anna passed. (no one else did)
> Anna **only** passed. (she did not get a high mark)
> We **only just** made it. (we barely made it)
> He **almost** failed every exam. / He failed **almost** every exam.
Comment adverbs (*Unfortunately, ... Probably, ...*) often come first, and focus adverbs stand next to the word they highlight.

## Common mistakes
- ~~She goes always to bed early.~~ → She **always goes** to bed early.
- ~~I have seen never such a mess.~~ → I have **never seen** such a mess.
- ~~He didn't know probably.~~ → He **probably didn't** know.
- ~~He opened carefully the door.~~ → He opened the door **carefully**.
structure:
## Схема позиций
| Позиция | Место | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| **Front** | перед подлежащим | **Fortunately,** nobody was hurt. |
| **Mid** (be) | после be | She is **always** polite. |
| **Mid** (aux) | после 1-го вспомогательного | He has **already** left. |
| **Mid** (verb) | перед смысловым глаголом | They **often** travel. |
| **End** | после глагола/дополнения | She replied **politely**. |

## Формулы
> подлежащее + (**наречие**) + глагол + дополнение + **способ** + **место** + **время**
> **be / aux + adverb**: is **never**, has **often**, will **probably**
> adverb **before** negative: **definitely** isn't, **probably** won't
> **hardly, scarcely** — after can / could: can **hardly** hear

## Типичные группы
| Группа | Примеры | Обычная позиция |
|---|---|---|
| Частота | always, usually, often, rarely, never | mid |
| Степень | almost, nearly, quite, hardly | mid, перед словом |
| Способ | carefully, slowly, well | end (mid — редко) |
| Место, время | here, abroad, yesterday | end / front |
| Комментарий | unfortunately, probably | front / mid |

exercises.title: Порядок слов: наречие и глагол
exercises.instruction: Поставьте слова из скобок в правильном порядке (вместе с наречием).
exercises.example: She (usually / doesn't) eat breakfast. → She **doesn't usually** eat breakfast.

items.text: I {{don't always|do not always}} agree with my manager.
The decision {{will probably be}} announced tomorrow.
I {{definitely don't|definitely do not}} want to move abroad.
She {{has always been}} generous with her time.
We {{were just leaving}} when the phone rang.
She {{carefully read}} the contract before signing it.
He {{can hardly}} hear anything from the back row.

exercises.title: Порядок в конце предложения
exercises.instruction: Поставьте слова в правильном порядке (способ — место — время; enough после прилагательного).

items.text: The room isn't {{big enough}} for twenty people.
He drove {{home carefully}} because of the ice.
They are meeting {{at the station tomorrow}}.
I {{still haven't|still have not}} received the invoice.
We have {{only just}} arrived, so we haven't unpacked.
He {{quietly closed}} the door and left.

items.why: Между глаголом и дополнением наречия нет; поэтому **carefully read the contract**.
Порядок в конце: способ → место → время: **calmly at the meeting yesterday**.
Наречие **ever** после подлежащего, перед смысловым глаголом.

items.q: The film ___ finished when we arrived.
She ___ managed to be there on time.

options: I never have been so embarrassed.
I have been never so embarrassed.
I have never been so embarrassed.
items.why: Перед смысловым причастием, после первого вспомогательного.

options: The conference will take next June place in Vienna.
The conference will take place in Vienna next June.
The conference will take place Vienna in next June.
items.why: Наречия не разрывают сочетание take place; в конце — место, потом время: **in Vienna next June**.

options: She is still waiting for an answer.
She still is waiting for an answer.
She is waiting still for an answer.
items.why: **still** — после be в составе is waiting.

options: He enjoyed very much the trip.
He enjoyed the trip very much.
items.why: Не между глаголом и дополнением; very без much не работает.

options: We go rarely to the cinema.
We rarely go to the cinema.
We go to rarely the cinema.

exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, поставив наречие из скобок на правильное место. Если допустимо несколько мест, достаточно одного.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями; следите за позицией наречий.

items.prompt: What do you always / never do before going to bed?
items.sample: I always check my email before bed, and I never drink coffee after six.

items.prompt: Describe how you usually travel to work or university (manner, place, time).
items.sample: I usually travel to work by tram, and I arrive at the office at about nine.

items.prompt: Write about something you have only just learned or finished.
items.sample: I have only just finished reading a very long novel.

items.prompt: What do you probably not do enough of?
items.sample: I probably don't exercise enough during the week.
